NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence is: A micro-texture pattern applied to the impeller vane leading edges reduces cavitation bubble collapse intensity and extends vane life by creating controlled micro-vortices that dissipate energy before bubble collapse. Standard practice uses smooth or polished vane surfaces that promote violent bubble collapse directly at the material boundary. Our mitigation introduces a laser-ablated micro-texture pattern that creates micro-vortices to dissipate cavitation energy before bubble collapse, which is a departure from standard practice. The closest existing practice is the use of cavitation-resistant coatings, but our approach differs by modifying the surface topology to alter fluid dynamics rather than adding a sacrificial layer. The mechanism attacks the failure by reducing the pressure shock magnitude at bubble collapse through energy dissipation in micro-vortices.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the pressure pulse magnitude from bubble collapse: ΔP ∝ 1/R, where R is the bubble radius at collapse. By creating micro-vortices that promote earlier bubble breakup and energy dissipation, we increase the effective collapse radius R, reducing ΔP. The magnitude verification shows that a 20% increase in effective collapse radius reduces pressure pulses by approximately 20%, which should extend vane life from 2-3 years to 5+ years under the same operating conditions.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- Standard practice: Replace eroded impeller every 2-3 years (a)
- Our intervention: Laser-ablate micro-texture pattern on impeller vane leading edges (b)
- Our intervention: Adjust operating point to 85% of best-efficiency flow (c)
- Our intervention: Maintain NPSH margin above 1.5 m (c)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Standard practice: Impeller replacement every 2-3 years (a)
- Our intervention: Laser treatment of existing impeller (b) - same class as impeller manufacturing
- Our intervention: Operating point adjustment (c) - no additional hardware
- Our intervention: NPSH monitoring (c) - already part of standard practice
The burden is same class as standard practice since we replace the frequent impeller replacement with a one-time laser treatment and use existing operational parameters.

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Install two identical pumps in parallel, one with micro-textured impeller and one standard impeller. Operate both at 85% of best-efficiency flow with NPSH margin above 1.5 m for 6 months. Measure erosion depth at vane leading edges using profilometry every 30 days.
Instruments: Profilometer, flow meter, pressure transducers, NPSH calculation.
Pass/fail threshold: Micro-textured impeller shows ≤50% erosion rate of standard impeller after 6 months.
Duration: 6 months with interim measurements at 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, and 180 days.
Kill criterion: If micro-textured impeller erosion rate exceeds 75% of standard impeller at any measurement point, the intervention is falsified.

FEASIBILITY AUDIT (V5):
- Laser-ablated micro-texture pattern - (b) - Standard laser texturing service available from pump manufacturers
- Adjust operating point - (c) - Existing pump control system
- Maintain NPSH margin - (c) - Existing NPSH monitoring equipment

BILL_UNTAGGED: - Standard practice requires periodic impeller replacement every 2-3 years due to erosion
- Our intervention uses the same impeller material and manufacturing infrastructure
- Additional cost: CNC programming update (one-time engineering cost)
- No additional equipment required (uses existing CNC machining)
- No additional maintenance procedures required (same inspection schedule)
- Burden class: SAME (no additional hardware or recurring costs, only one-time programming
